key_findings: The World's Columbian Exposition (Chicago World's Fair) was held from May 1 to October 30, 1893, according to [web-5fbfeb3f554e] (Wikipedia) and [web-05a1fe536568] (official directory), and the second day of the fair, May 2, 1893, was reported in the New York Times article [web-0cf2e9da0b18] as showing a dramatic falloff in attendance compared to opening day.

The New York Times article [web-0cf2e9da0b18] contrasts the first day attendance of 'over 500,000 people' with the second day's attendance of 'less than 50,000,' but the exact numerical figure for the second Tuesday's attendance is not provided in the available text; the article snippet is truncated at 'Only ...' and does not give the precise number.
